rationale: Lens: scope, split and count honesty, round 5 at 7404845f, re-read from disk (spec.md only; ADRs unchanged since 4c46cf64). Both round-4 asks are ADDRESSED: F4 runs the Spec-125 R5(d) net-effect/revert test at the CURRENT tip on every read-back and AC-11 (xiv) pins accepted-then-reverted → FAIL; R4.1 now says 'plan-FORM (i)' / 'does not have the plan-bead form' and carries a dedicated hint for a closed plan-form dependency that plan.md does not map. The a593792a..7404845f regression check in this lens is clean: no deliverable moves between 129, the follow-on spec and 130; every new mechanism (readiness.PlanMapsBead shared with MF-1, the lazy plan.md read via git from internal/next, the audited tuple keys, ReattestStateUnlandedReview and the new ReattestStateMultipleFallbackCandidates, F1–F5 at read time) lands in files already In Scope, and the new audit keys have a documented home because the existing reattest keys live in workflow/{architecture,interfaces,runbook}.md and core/USAGE.md, all already on R6.5's surface list. Attacks: the audited tuple cannot be forged into a PASS that reattest itself would refuse, because F1–F5 are re-derived from git and the panel scan on every read and the residual is now stated as a new bounded reach rather than 'the same class'; the anchor/round rule cannot be defeated by an unlanded round masquerading as an anchor's ancestor, since any ancestor of the second parent is reachable from the tip and therefore landed by definition; PlanMapsBead is honest about positional counting and agrees with MF-1 by construction. Two minor honesty gaps remain, neither changing the design: the F2 residual names only the metadata forge, although anchors and rounds come from agent-writable panel.json and one forged high-round exact-match registration disables F2 (the same class as item (c)'s forged exact match confirming on the primary path); and the '7–10 beads' estimate has not moved across five rounds of scope growth and now understates R1, R4 and R6 taken together.
concrete_changes_required: State the panel-side residual beside the metadata-forge residual in R4.2: F2's anchors and rounds are read from agent-writable panel.json registrations (ADR-0037 §8), so a single forged registration with a high `round` and `reviewed_head_sha` equal to the candidate's second parent makes every real later unlanded round pass F2, at reattest time and at read time. Say that this is the same class as a forged exact-match `reviewed_head_sha` confirming a primary-path candidate under item (c), that it is detectable by inspection of the registration dir, and that F1, F3 and F4 (git-derived) are unaffected by it.

Revise the bead estimate or say the relief valve is expected. '7–10 beads' has been repeated unchanged since round 1 while R1 gained seven near-miss classes, R1.8's dispatch rewrite and the git-backed plan read; R4 gained F1–F5 at acceptance and at read time, the audited tuple and two reattest states; R6 gained per-record digests and MF-4 occurrence identity. Counted honestly R1 is 2–3 beads, R4 is 3, R6 is 2–3, R2/R3/R5 2–3 together: 9–12. Either state 9–12, or keep 7–10 and say in OQ-1 that the plan gate should expect the R6 split to fire.

findings.title: NEW_ISSUE — F2's residual omits the panel-side forge
findings.detail: R4.2's 'Residual, stated honestly' covers the metadata forge of the binding and audit tuple and correctly says F1–F5 bound it to what reattest would accept. But F2 itself reads anchors and rounds from panel.json registrations, which are agent-writable files (internal/panel/panel.go; ADR-0037 §8). A forged registration dir with `round: 99` and `reviewed_head_sha` = the candidate's second parent is an anchor at round 99, so any genuine later unlanded round (O3's round-2/round-3 shapes) has a lower round and F2 passes — at reattest time and on every read-back. This does not break the design: it is exactly the class the repo already accepts for item (c), where a forged exact-match `reviewed_head_sha` CONFIRMS a primary-path candidate outright, and F1 (single candidate), F3 (surviving tip) and F4 (net-effect) are git-derived and unaffected. It should simply be stated next to the metadata residual so the ADR-0041 amendment's threat statement is complete. On the BRIEF's specific question — can a later unlanded round masquerade as an anchor's ANCESTOR? — no: an ancestor of the second parent is an ancestor of the merge, which is reachable from the tip, so it is landed by definition; the only masquerade is the forged anchor above.

findings.title: NEW_ISSUE — the '7–10 beads' estimate has not moved while the scope has
findings.detail: Count honesty is this lens's core question. The estimate was written at round 1 for a spec with a one-predicate R1, a corroboration-only R4.2 and a Detail-digest R6. At 7404845f: R1 has seven near-miss classes with a classification order, two N2b sub-cases, N4 with lineage/no-lineage arms, R1.8 (a)–(d) including spec-branch resolution and dispatch-into-T, and a lazy two-source plan read; R4 has membership (R4.1), the finder plus F1–F5 at acceptance AND read time, the audited tuple and validity contract, two new reattest states, set semantics in two functions, binding-veto-vs-repair, arm 1b with precedence, and #232's disposition; R6 has the scoped flag with NoOptDefVal handling, evidence I/O, schema v2 with per-record digests and MF-4 occurrence identity, the validator, ready-check read-back with mixed-coverage recovery, and the skill/doc sweep. Spec 128 planned 10 beads for a smaller surface. An honest plan-time range is 9–12, and the R6 relief valve should be described as expected rather than conditional. No split is required by this reviewer; the number should be.

findings.title: Audited tuple, anchor/round rule and PlanMapsBead attacked — hold
findings.detail: Tuple: a forged audit must equal the binding pair AND the single scan-derived candidate, and F1–F5 are re-derived from git/panel on each read, so the forge reaches only a real, reachable, source-named, single, non-reverted merge with no visible later unlanded round — the spec now calls this a new bounded reach, not 'the same class' (O3r4.1 honoured). A stale audit after an executor rewrite names a different pair and grants nothing (AC-11 xii). Round rule: with in-place round bumping (panel.go: 'Round and ReviewedHeadSHA are bumped IN THE SAME WRITE') a bead normally has ONE registration; O3's shape then has no anchor while a non-ancestor exists → fail closed → refuse, which is correct; the per-round-dir shape is handled by the greater-than rule with ties and missing rounds failing closed. The equal-OR-ancestor anchor is necessary, not a loosening: in #233's shape the second parent is complete's tree-identical commit, so equal-only would refuse every normal bead that later lands off the first-parent chain. PlanMapsBead: positional count AND chunk id, shared with evaluateMF1 by construction; AC-1's non-contiguous 1–7,12 fixture pins the positional semantics honestly rather than hiding them; a stale checkout plan.md makes a newly added plan bead N4 from that checkout, which is the same answer readiness gives from that checkout, so selection and readiness still agree.
